text:
jamie_support: customer on iOS reports SSE session returns a partial JSON response then connection closes when they switch from WiFi -> cellular. app shows a half-formed assistant reply, then spinner. they sent a packet capture and a repro video. asking for triage.
tyler_mobile: repro steps from the user: 1) open chat, 2) start generation (15-25s), 3) toggle hotspot/wifi while stream active. result: stream cuts with a partial data chunk, app reconnects and sometimes receives the same partial chunk again, then final abort. seems mobile-specific but reproduced on a Pixel as well.

alex_platform: do logs show 401 or token errors around reconnect? or is it straight TCP close/ECONNRESET?

maria_sre: check proxy/runtime logs for conn id 0x7f9a3b. we see immediate ECONNRESET on the TCP flow after the device IP changes. runtime also logged this around the same time:
```
[2026-02-18T14:02:11.123Z] conn=0x7f9a3b stream_id=987 seq=42 wrote=512 partial=true
[2026-02-18T14:02:11.125Z] conn=0x7f9a3b tcp=ECONNRESET peer=10.4.2.14
[2026-02-18T14:02:11.130Z] stream_resume_candidate request_id=abc-123 seq_start=42
```
this matches the duplicate-partial symptom: runtime kept the last emitted chunk in memory and when the client reconnects with a new TCP session, the gateway attempts a resume path that re-emits that partial chunk.

jamie_support: customer needs a mitigation now. any quick client-side suggestions I can give?

alex_platform: short-term: tell the client to (a) add a unique X-Request-ID per user request, (b) on reconnect send Last-Event-ID or X-Last-Seq (sequence id) to the server so server can dedupe, (c) treat identical seq IDs as duplicates and drop them. also suggest enabling a keepalive ping (every 10-15s) so mobile NATs/proxies are less likely to close mid-chunk. example curl to simulate:
```bash
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "X-Request-ID: test-req-01" \
     "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-stream" \\
     --no-buffer
```
then flip wifi to hotspot after stream starts.

tyler_mobile: we ran that on a debug build. confirmed: when the client reconnects and sends the same request-id but without last-seq, server replays seq=42 chunk and client UI merges it again causing duplicate partial text. adding last-seq check on client fixed UX (ignore seq <= seen_seq).

maria_sre: long-term ops/eng mitigation ideas: (1) runtime should emit an explicit final chunk marker for each logical token batch (last-chunk=true) so clients can detect truncated final chunks; (2) persist recent request_id -> highest_seq for ~30s to dedupe resume replays; (3) make resume protocol require Last-Event-ID to confirm resume offset, otherwise start fresh stream. opening INF ticket for these.

alex_platform: filed INF-5821 to track: add last-chunk marker + short-lived resume cache + stronger resume handshake. will add canary to dedicated region so we can validate on mobile repro cases.

jamie_support: thanks. i'll reply to the customer with the immediate client workaround (X-Request-ID + Last-Seq + keepalive) and offer a test build. @maria_sre can you attach the conn logs to INF-5821? :thumbsup:
\mtimeout-bot: reminder set — follow up with customer in 48h if no response.

jamie_support: great, closing loop after we confirm the canary.
